pattern_id: BoundedExecutor head-of-line blocking causes network starvation to all validators
description: BUG PATTERN: Network Starvation from BoundedExecutor Head-of-Line Blocking. DESCRIPTION: Using one BoundedExecutor per destination validator causes network starvation. When the executor for one specific validator runs out of tickets, the send_message operation becomes blocking. If this blocking operation exists in a shared code path (e.g., helper handling PayloadAvailabilityRequest or CertificatesRequest), it blocks message sending to ALL validators, not just the overloaded one. ROOT CAUSE: The BoundedExecutor design creates per-destination blocking that propagates to shared code paths. When one destination is slow or unresponsive, the blocking wait for permits causes head-of-line blocking affecting all other destinations. FIX: For UnreliableNetwork, drop messages to overloaded peers instead of blocking. For ReliableNetwork, use spawn_with_permit to preemptively acquire permits before entering tokio::select branches. LESSON: Per-destination resource limits (like executor permits) must not block shared code paths. Use non-blocking alternatives (try_acquire, drop on failure) for unreliable paths, and pre-acquire resources before entering multiplexed select branches for reliable paths.
